body.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). If \(((P_{r,\theta_r},D_r,\theta_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), then the pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_{r,\theta_r})_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed intervention-contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the truncated-factorization functional at \(V_{i_X}\).
body.justification: After the separate \(p\geq2\) graph-transfer theorem, this result uses \(p\geq3\) only to transfer an identified polynomial-CPCM law and graph to one treatment and two response contrasts.
body.gap: The published direct-law CPCM theorem identifies the DAG but neither unpools labeled type laws nor proves that the strict polynomial subclass's support, modular factorization, and moments make the designated contrast functional identifiable.
body.consumer: It states the intervention-effect output available to a prospective known-composition bulk assay after broad graph recovery, without extending finite-grid, certification, or Wald claims beyond the strict polynomial subclass.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a type \(r\), and write \(V_r=(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp})\) for a generic cellular vector with law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\). Its endogenous variables are the labeled count coordinates \(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp}\); the treatment is \(V_{r i_X}\), and the two outcomes are \(V_{r i_Y}\) and \(V_{r i_Z}\). The polynomial CPCM is causally sufficient, so there is no latent common cause among these endogenous coordinates.

First distinguish recovery of an observational law from identification of a causal functional. Let \(H(z)=(H_1(z),\ldots,H_J(z))^{\mathsf T}\) denote the observable row-PGF vector. Membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), together with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), permits application of \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\), which yields
\[
 (G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}
 =\mathscr R_M(H)(z)
 =\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\},
 \qquad z\in(0,1]^p, \tag{2}
\]
and PGF coefficient uniqueness identifies every labeled observational law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\). Thus (2) is an equality between an observable recovery functional and component PGFs; it does not define an intervention law.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}polynomial\text{-}class\text{-}inclusion}\), every recovered polynomial-CPCM component has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\). Since \(p\geq3\) implies \(p\geq2\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\) identifies its labeled DAG \(D_r\). This invokes the broad graph result only after its own hypotheses have been verified; the ordered embedding \(\iota\) is not needed for that graph-identification step.

Full support supplies the overlap needed to identify every observational kernel. Indeed, for any parent configuration \(a\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|}\), completing the other coordinates by zeros gives one vector in \(\mathbb N_0^p\) having positive \(P_{r,\theta_r}\)-mass. Hence
\[
 P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)>0. \tag{3}
\]
The identified law and graph therefore determine
\[
 p_{rs,\theta_r}(v_s\mid a)
 =
 \frac{P_{r,\theta_r}(V_{rs}=v_s,
          V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a)}
      {P_{r,\theta_r}(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a)}. \tag{4}
\]
The denominator is positive by (3); for a root it is the mass of the unique empty configuration, namely one.

We next derive the causal law represented by the truncated product. In the causally sufficient acyclic CPCM, generate the coordinates in a topological order using mutually independent node noises and the identified kernels (4). Under \(\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=x)\), intervention modularity replaces only the assignment for \(V_{r i_X}\) by the constant \(x\in\{1,2\}\). Conditional multiplication in that topological order gives
\[
 P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=x)}(v_{-i_X})
 =\prod_{s\ne i_X}
 p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
 v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)
 \Big|_{v_{i_X}=x}. \tag{5}
\]
This product is a probability mass function, rather than merely a formal expression. All its terms are nonnegative. Sum successively in reverse topological order over the nonintervened vertices. When a current terminal vertex is summed out, no remaining factor depends on its value, while its own conditional mass function sums to one. Repetition leaves total mass one. This also establishes (5) directly from the structural intervention semantics, rather than defining the causal target to equal an arbitrary observable expression.

It remains to justify the expectations in the contrast. If \(N\mid\lambda\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), then for every integer \(\ell\geq0\), direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(N)_\ell\mid\lambda]
 =\sum_{n=\ell}^{\infty}\frac{n!}{(n-\ell)!}
   e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^n}{n!}
 =\lambda^\ell, \tag{6}
\]
where \((N)_\ell=N(N-1)\cdots(N-\ell+1)\). For every integer \(m\geq0\), the finite identity
\(N^m=\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}S(m,\ell)(N)_\ell\), with \(S(m,\ell)\) the Stirling numbers of the second kind, shows from (6) that \(\mathbb E[N^m\mid\lambda]\) is a finite polynomial in \(\lambda\).

Under either intervention, the coordinate \(V_{r i_X}=x\) has moments of every order. All nonintervened root coordinates have fixed positive Poisson rates and hence have moments of every order by (6). Suppose inductively that every parent of a nonintervened node \(s\) has moments of every order. The positive-polynomial rate assumption and the fixed positive-integer exponent assumption give
\[
 \lambda_{rs,\theta_r}
 =\alpha_{rs}+
 \sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
 b_{rsk}V_{rk}^{q_{sk}}. \tag{7}
\]
For \(m\geq1\), writing \(h=1+|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|\), convexity yields
\[
 \lambda_{rs,\theta_r}^{m}
 \leq h^{m-1}\!\left(
 \alpha_{rs}^{m}+
 \sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
 b_{rsk}^{m}V_{rk}^{m q_{sk}}
 \right). \tag{8}
\]
Every term on the right has finite expectation by the induction hypothesis, including when a parent is the fixed intervention coordinate. Equations (6)--(8) imply that \(V_{rs}\) has moments of every order. Induction along the finite acyclic graph proves in particular that \(V_{r i_Y}\) and \(V_{r i_Z}\) have finite first moments under both interventions.

Finally, every factor on the right of (5) is identified by (4), and its graph indices are identified by \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\). Therefore summing \((v_{i_Y},v_{i_Z})\) against (5) at \(x=2\) and subtracting the corresponding sum at \(x=1\) yields an observable functional. By (5) and the established integrability, this functional equals
\[
 \bigl(\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}\bigr)
 =\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=2)}}
      [(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]
  -\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=1)}}
      [(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]. \tag{9}
\]
Applying (9) for every labeled type \(r=1,\ldots,K\) identifies \(\boldsymbol\tau\). The assumptions \(p\geq3\) and the fixed embedding \(\iota\) enter only in selecting the one treatment and two response coordinates in (9); broad CPCM graph recovery is supplied separately by \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\) under \(p\geq2\).
